newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FDA clears Premier Laser for tooth treatment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FDA clears Premier Laser for tooth treatment.

text.p: U.S. medical authorities said on Wednesday they had cleared for marketing the "erbium YAG" laser system made by Premier Laser Systems Inc. for the treatment of tooth decay.

The Food and Drug Administration said the approval of the laser was the first cleared for use directly on teeth. Lasers previously had been approved only for dental use on soft tissue such as the gums.

"Use of lasers in dentistry is medicine for the 21st century. They will give dentists and patients a significant new option for treating decay and doing other related procedures," said Bruce Burlington, director of the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health.
The FDA said that studies by the manufacturer showed the laser is as safe and effective as a high speed drill for removing dental decay and preparing a cavity for a filling.
It said the manufacturer's study indicated that fewer patients needed anesthetic for pain.
The agency said the laser was reported to be noisy, but the noise was different from that of a standard drill.
It added that the laser was also cleared to roughen the enamel, a procedure used to improve bonding of the restoration.
